Welcome to Indie App Spotlight. This is 9to5Mac's weekly series that brings you the latest from the world of independent apps. If you're a developer and want your app to be featured, please get in touch.

On Apple TV, games are often not the first thing on developers' minds. Compared with iPhone, iPad and even Mac, the game selection on Apple TV is not that extensive. Fortunately, CloudGear, a one-stop platform, neatly brings all the major cloud gaming services together under a single interface. It also works on iPhone and iPad.

Key features

CloudGear supports all the major cloud gaming platforms, including GeForce Now, Xbox Cloud Streaming, Amazon Luna and Boosteroid. It can stream at up to 5K resolution and 120FPS, and supports HDR, 10-bit colour as well as Dolby 7.1 surround sound.

Beyond those specs, CloudGear also offers a number of thoughtful features. It supports controller rumble — and if your controller doesn't have rumble, it will fall back to the iPhone's Taptic Engine. Users can also hand off games from the iPhone or iPad app to Apple TV, so you don't have to hunt through your TV to find the game you want.

On iPhone and iPad, CloudGear offers a Home Screen widget that lets you bookmark games and jump straight in without any extra steps.

Finally, CloudGear supports connecting iPhone-compatible AR glasses, such as XREAL glasses, so you can play games on a big screen right in front of your eyes.

Download the app

CloudGear is available for free on the App Store, supporting iPhone and iPad running iOS 17.6 and later, as well as Apple TV running tvOS 18.6 and later. To unlock the full feature set, subscriptions are available at US$1.99 per month or US$14.99 per year, or you can purchase a perpetual licence for US$39.99. Subscribers get a 7-day free trial. Check out the official website for more details.
